title: Priority Print Spooler
instructions:
Implement `PrintSpooler` and `validate_job` in `spooler.py`. Jobs are processed one page
per tick. Higher numeric priority wins; ties use original submission order. Once started,
a job prints without preemption until finished or canceled, regardless of new submissions.

`validate_job(name: str, pages: int, priority: int) -> None` raises `ValueError` unless
name is a nonempty string, pages is a positive integer (not bool), and priority is any
integer (not bool). Whitespace names are valid.

`PrintSpooler()` starts empty. Implement:
- `submit(name: str, pages: int, priority: int = 0) -> int`: validate, enqueue, and return
  a unique sequential ID starting at 1. Invalid submissions do not consume IDs.
- `cancel(job_id: int) -> bool`: discard an active or queued job and return True; return
  False for unknown, finished, or already canceled IDs.
- `reprioritize(job_id: int, priority: int) -> bool`: validate priority first (same rule
  as above). Change priority only for a queued job and return True, without changing its
  tie-breaking submission order. Active or unknown IDs return False.
- `tick() -> dict | None`: if idle, start the best queued job. Print exactly one page and
  return `{'id': int, 'name': str, 'page': int, 'total': int, 'done': bool}`, where page
  is the one-based page just printed. A finished job is removed immediately. Do not start
  another job in that same tick. Return None when no work exists.
- `snapshot() -> dict`: return `{'active': record_or_None, 'queued': [records...]}` with
  queued jobs in dispatch order. A record has exactly `id`, `name`, `pages`, `priority`,
  `printed` (pages printed so far). Return independent dict/list copies.
Job ID arguments are integers. Invalid input errors must not alter spooler state.

## Files
- `spooler.py`
